findings.question: q-chemistry-mixtures-and-separation-0013
findings.quote: This reverses the balance. Strong holding by the paper shortens travel. Check which is stronger, the solvent's carrying or the paper's holding.
findings.problem: The note identifies the reversed balance and gives a check, but does not explain why this choice looks right. For example, a student may think stronger attraction to the paper helps pull the dye upward; saying that strong holding shortens travel corrects that idea without identifying its appeal.
findings.fix: Add why it looks right: 'The dye travels along the paper, so stronger attraction may seem to help it climb.' Keep the mistake and check.
